basis: Defined by skeletal muscle trigger points and myofascial dysfunction; referred pain does not establish nerve damage.
Disordered calcium sensing causes hypocalcemia and hypercalciuria; nephrocalcinosis occurs in 12/27 (~44%), although treatment can contribute.
Malignant glandular epithelial tumour originating in the urinary bladder.
Proximal tubular bicarbonate wasting causes metabolic acidosis; reduced bone density is reported, but its frequency is insufficiently established.
Clonal malignancy of blood and marrow cells; additional organ damage is not shared consistently across this umbrella.
Syphilitic CNS infection with meningeal or cerebrospinal fluid abnormalities despite absence of clinical neurologic symptoms.
Mitochondrial dysfunction underlies the listed subtypes; cardiomyopathy and leukoencephalopathy define different presentations, without a shared organ phenotype.
Bacterial infection umbrella; no anatomical site is consistently affected across the group.
Nonsyndromic intellectual disability with developmental impairment; no demonstrated systemic metabolic disease.
Defining cerebral and cerebellar malformations with severe developmental impairment; ocular and skeletal findings have sparse 1/1 reports, not reliable cohort frequencies.
Inflammation affects a spinal nerve root; the umbrella does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated cause.
Reduced cerebrospinal fluid pressure is a CNS disorder; occasional hearing symptoms do not establish common lasting ear damage.
Defined by hypoplastic distal phalanges and shortened metacarpals.
Inherited cobalamin-processing defect causing isolated methylmalonic acidemia; common direct neurologic or renal injury is not established for this subtype.
HSV causes direct vesicular and ulcerative mucocutaneous infection; encephalitis and keratitis affect minority subgroups.
Severe congenital skeletal myopathy defines the syndrome; respiratory insufficiency chiefly reflects muscle weakness. Genital malformations have no dedicated axis.
Sensorineural hearing loss and vestibular hyporeflexia affect the inner ear; speech delay is secondary to hearing impairment.
Defined by muscular dystrophy and abnormal muscle histology; internalized capillaries do not establish vascular disease or common cardiomyopathy.
Metabolic disease with defining encephalopathy and deafness; hepatic failure is frequent (30–79%). Optic atrophy is occasional (5–29%).
Skeletal dysplasia; myopia, hearing impairment and cleft palate each occur frequently (30–79%). Retinal detachment and cataract are occasional.
Defining gingival fibromatosis and progressive sensorineural hearing loss; both occur in 80–99%.
Neurodevelopmental impairment affects most; hepatic dysfunction and coagulation-factor deficiencies commonly exceed 30%, especially in predominant PMM2-CDG.
Neurodevelopmental disease with regression, absent speech and central hypotonia; muscle weakness does not establish a separate myopathy.
Inherited increased bone sclerosis; marrow failure and cranial nerve injury are subtype-dependent rather than shared across the umbrella.
Congenital partial or complete absence of the radius with associated hand and thumb skeletal abnormalities.
